reason: The base alloy's precipitate formation and radiation tolerance are directly supported by E1/E2. The Hf effect on precipitate suppression is supported by E1's mention of W29Ta42Cr5V16Hf8 showing no precipitates at 10 dpa, but the mechanism of Hf reducing Cr/V diffusion is not directly evidenced in the cited passages. The claim that Hf doping retains manufacturability is unsupported by any cited evidence.
premises: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 forms Cr-V-rich precipitates at ~8 dpa at 1073 K
Hf addition suppresses Cr-V precipitate formation in a related W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy at 10 dpa
Hf atoms introduce lattice distortions and reduce Cr/V diffusion via size mismatch and high melting point
The base alloy shows negligible irradiation hardening and no dislocation loops up to 8 dpa
Hf doping will not compromise bulk manufacturability or single-phase BCC structure
